Jonas / Ava —

Root-cause update from the Rate & Edge teams (summary):
- At 15:47 PDT a config push introduced a per-tenant burst accounting change that flips the burst credit aggregation from cluster-global -> tenant-scoped. The aim was to prevent noisy neighbors from burning shared burst credits.
- Unfortunately the new accounting path didn't migrate a safety clamp that prevents negative credit reconciliation. Rapid short bursts from Clarity's ingest pattern produced a reconciliation loop. That loop caused the edge to mark requests as "burst window exceeded" and fall back to a hard reject path (503) while simultaneously increasing tail latency due to requeue/backpressure.
- We also saw a policy gating bug that applied the updated guardrail to an older legacy-rate-table for Clarity (an unintended mapping), meaning their effective burst bucket was far smaller than intended.

Attachments: quota_policy_snapshot_20270503.yaml (snapshot of effective policy), small request trace bundle attached in the drive link.

Proposed immediate actions (we can do within 20 mins after approvals):
1) Emergency rollback of the burst-accounting change for affected US-west edge nodes (full rollback window ~10m to propagate).
2) Patch that restores the safety-clamp in the reconciliation flow (hotfix planned and tested locally).
3) Manual credit top-up for Clarity to clear queued work and avoid data-loss while we stabilize.
4) Post-mortem and a targeted canary to reintroduce per-tenant accounting with the clamp enabled.

We recommend authorization for (1) + (3) now. If approved I'll coordinate the rollback and confirm when the cluster shows normalized 2xx rates.

Neha Kapoor
Senior SRE — Redwood Inference
[Related link: JIRA-OPS-1947]
[Attachment referenced: quota_policy_snapshot_20270503.yaml]
